s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear
key_facts: Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Lytic bony lesions on CT scan of pelvis
Hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet

Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, and multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material on biopsy

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, and lytic bony lesions

shortlist.label: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear

raw.rationale: The presence of hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and a hypercellular bone marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction are key findings that strongly support the diagnosis of multiple myeloma. Additionally, the abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses and the monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, these findings can be associated with multiple myeloma, and the other key findings in this case more strongly support multiple myeloma as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with IgM monoclonal protein, which is not mentioned in the case, and the bone marrow findings are more consistent with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Plasmacytoma is a solitary tumor of plasma cells, but the widespread bone marrow involvement and multiple lytic lesions in this case suggest a more systemic disease, such as multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While mixed cryoglobulinemia can present with skin lesions and elevated cryoglobulins, the presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein and the bone marrow findings in this case more strongly support multiple myeloma as the primary diagnosis.
